hint: A president delivered an address dedicating a battlefield cemetery
funFact: Did you know? Lincoln's Gettysburg Address was just 272 words. The speaker before him, Edward Everett, spoke for 2 hours. Nobody remembers Everett's speech.

hint: An automobile company was incorporated that would change industry
funFact: Did you know? Ford Motor Company was incorporated with $28,000 in capital. Within 5 years, it was the largest carmaker in the world. The Model T would arrive in 1908.

hint: The largest naval battle of WWI raged in the North Sea
funFact: Did you know? Jutland was the largest naval battle of WWI — 250 ships. Both sides claimed victory. Historians still argue who actually won.

hint: London's worst pea-souper killed thousands and led to clean air laws
funFact: Did you know? The Great Smog of London killed 4,000 people in 5 days — possibly 12,000 total. It was so thick, people couldn't see their own feet. It led to the UK Clean Air Act.

hint: Military prisoners tunnelled out in a daring camp escape
event: The Great Escape from Stalag Luft III
funFact: Did you know? The Great Escape tunnel was 9 metres deep and 111 metres long. 76 prisoners escaped; 73 were recaptured; 50 were executed. The 3 who made it home walked for weeks.

hint: A lawyer was thrown off a train in South Africa, igniting activism
event: Gandhi's train incident in South Africa
funFact: Did you know? Gandhi was thrown off a train in South Africa for refusing to leave first class. The incident radicalised him. 50 years later, it helped end the British Raj.

hint: A diabetic boy received the first injection that would save his life
funFact: Did you know? The first insulin patient was a 14-year-old boy. He went from near-death to thriving within days. His diabetes had been a death sentence — no longer.

hint: A Scottish inventor demonstrated pictures transmitted by wire
funFact: Did you know? Baird's first TV image was the face of a ventriloquist's dummy — more reliable than a person for repeated test runs. Low-budget TV, 1925 edition.

hint: A theoretical physicist was born who would redefine the universe
funFact: Did you know? Einstein failed his first university entrance exam. He was 16. He also famously struggled with language as a child — some teachers thought he was slow.

hint: A host nation won football's greatest prize in its own capital
event: France wins the 1998 FIFA World Cup
funFact: Did you know? France won the 1998 World Cup as host — their first win, led by Zidane's two headers in the final. The Champs-Élysées held 1.5 million celebrating fans.

hint: A revolution triumphed after guerrillas marched into a capital
funFact: Did you know? The Cuban Revolution's final blow came when Batista fled to the Dominican Republic at 3 AM — bringing $300 million in a plane. Castro entered Havana 8 days later.

hint: A physicist accidentally discovered rays that could see through skin
funFact: Did you know? Röntgen called them 'X-rays' because X means 'unknown' in maths. He used his own wife's hand for the first image. She allegedly said: 'I have seen my death!'

hint: A moving assembly line transformed automobile manufacturing
event: Ford introduces the moving assembly line
funFact: Did you know? Ford's assembly line cut Model T production from 12 hours to 90 minutes. Wages doubled, prices halved. Everyone wins. Except bicycle manufacturers.

hint: A council opened that would modernize the Catholic Church
funFact: Did you know? Vatican II reformed the Catholic Mass — moving it from Latin to local languages. For many Catholics, the first Mass they understood was in their 30s.

hint: Global stock markets crashed as a financial crisis deepened
funFact: Did you know? The 2008 crash wiped out $1.2 trillion of US stock value in a single day — the biggest point drop in Dow history at the time.

hint: A declaration offered the crown on condition of shared power
funFact: Did you know? The Declaration of Right predates the US Bill of Rights by over a century — and it's still on the books today. It limits the monarchy to this day.

hint: A privateer completed the second circumnavigation of the globe
funFact: Did you know? Drake returned to Plymouth in his ship Golden Hind loaded with Spanish treasure. Elizabeth I got a cut — enough to wipe out England's entire national debt.

hint: A science fiction show premiered that would run for 60 years
funFact: Did you know? Doctor Who's first episode aired the day after JFK's assassination — and was overshadowed by the news. The BBC quietly repeated it a week later.

hint: A massive explosion flattened forest across a Siberian landscape
funFact: Did you know? Tunguska flattened 2,000 sq km of Siberian forest — yet nobody even visited the site until 1927. Tsarist Russia had a lot going on.

hint: A rigid airship completed its first flight over a German lake
funFact: Did you know? The first Zeppelin flew for just 17 minutes before landing. It would take another 4 years before they became reliable. The Hindenburg disaster came 37 years later.

hint: A balloon made of cloth and paper rose above a French square
funFact: Did you know? The Montgolfier balloon's first 'passengers' were a sheep, a duck, and a rooster — to test if living things could survive at altitude. They all came back fine.

hint: A grand exhibition opened in a crystal palace in London
funFact: Did you know? The Great Exhibition's Crystal Palace was made of 1 million sq ft of glass — then the largest glass structure ever built. It burned down in 1936.

hint: An archbishop calculated creation began on this day
event: Ussher's creation date for the world
funFact: Did you know? Ussher calculated Earth's creation to October 23, 4004 BC, at 6pm. He used genealogies in the Bible. Modern geologists settle for 'around 4.5 billion years'.

hint: A British explorer became the first European to reach Hawaiian shores
funFact: Did you know? Captain Cook was killed by Hawaiians in 1779 — just a year after reaching Hawaii. His death involved a fight over a stolen boat. Cultural misunderstandings escalate.

hint: Two scientists announced the double helix structure of life
event: Watson and Crick discover DNA structure
funFact: Did you know? Watson and Crick figured out DNA's double helix using photograph 51 — a crucial X-ray by Rosalind Franklin. She didn't get the Nobel; she'd died by 1962.

hint: A year without a summer began after a massive volcanic eruption
funFact: Did you know? The Year Without a Summer was caused by Mount Tambora erupting the year before. Crops failed worldwide. Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein that summer — stuck indoors.

hint: A tunnel under the English Channel was formally opened
funFact: Did you know? The Channel Tunnel is 31 miles long — with 23 miles under the seabed. 10 workers died building it. It's the world's longest undersea rail tunnel.

hint: A president declared that slaves in rebel states would be freed
funFact: Did you know? The preliminary Emancipation Proclamation freed no one immediately — it only promised to free slaves in states still in rebellion after 100 days. The final version came January 1, 1863.

hint: A president asked Congress to declare war on an empire
funFact: Did you know? FDR's 'Day of Infamy' speech was literally written the night before on a legal pad. The original text was 'date which will live in world history' — he crossed it out and wrote 'infamy'.

hint: A Frankish king was crowned emperor by the pope on Christmas Day
funFact: Did you know? Charlemagne was crowned on Christmas Day and was reportedly surprised by it — the Pope placed the crown without warning. It's still debated whether he really was.
